description: A single table rendered as an image (no plots, spectra or micrographs), captioned as a comparison of inference time and segmentation performance. It has five columns: Dataset, Method, Metric, Segmentation performance and Inference time per image (ms). Two dataset blocks are evaluated. The first block is LCS (1360 × 600) (Polycrystalline), scored by ARI, listing Watershed 0.54 / 6.12 ms, OTSU 0.64 / 4.54 ms, Canny 0.73 / 16.48 ms, SAM 0.86 / 1850.35 ms and MatSAM 0.96 / 1926.35 ms. The second block is NBS-1 (512 × 512) (Multiphase), scored by IoU, listing OTSU 0.75 / 0.53 ms, Adaptive 0.45 / 0.58 ms, SAM 0.85 / 1575.24 ms and MatSAM 0.91 / 1812.67 ms. Bold entries mark the best value in each column: MatSAM's segmentation scores (0.96 ARI, 0.91 IoU) and OTSU's inference times (4.54 ms, 0.53 ms). The table's argument is that MatSAM yields the highest segmentation accuracy on both datasets, outperforming classical methods and SAM, but that this accuracy comes at a large inference-time cost, the deep-learning methods being roughly three orders of magnitude slower than OTSU.

observations.observation: The figure is a single tabular comparison with columns Dataset, Method, Metric, Segmentation performance and Inference time per image (ms).
On LCS (1360 × 600) (Polycrystalline), scored by ARI, segmentation performance is Watershed 0.54, OTSU 0.64, Canny 0.73, SAM 0.86 and MatSAM 0.96, so MatSAM is the highest.
On NBS-1 (512 × 512) (Multiphase), scored by IoU, segmentation performance is OTSU 0.75, Adaptive 0.45, SAM 0.85 and MatSAM 0.91, so MatSAM is the highest.
The evaluation metric differs by dataset: ARI for LCS and IoU for NBS-1.
LCS inference times are Watershed 6.12 ms, OTSU 4.54 ms, Canny 16.48 ms, SAM 1850.35 ms and MatSAM 1926.35 ms, so OTSU is fastest and MatSAM slowest.
NBS-1 inference times are OTSU 0.53 ms, Adaptive 0.58 ms, SAM 1575.24 ms and MatSAM 1812.67 ms, so OTSU is fastest and MatSAM slowest.
Bold entries in the segmentation column are MatSAM's scores (0.96 on LCS, 0.91 on NBS-1); bold entries in the inference-time column are OTSU's times (4.54 ms on LCS, 0.53 ms on NBS-1).
The caption states that bold values indicate the best results.
The caption states this is inference time and corresponding segmentation performance of MatSAM and other methods on the public LCS and NBS-1 datasets.
SAM and MatSAM, the deep-learning methods, are roughly three orders of magnitude slower than OTSU (e.g. 1850-1926 ms vs 4.54 ms on LCS).
